meta.scope: California property tax rules that govern what happens to Property A (Cupertino / Santa Clara County) and Property B (San Francisco) on a transfer into or out of a trust, and on inheritance.

rows.label: Maximum ad valorem property tax rate
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization
rows.note: Counties add voter-approved debt service on top. San Francisco's verified total for FY2025-26 is 1.18268325%.

rows.label: Event that resets assessed value to current market value
rows.value: Change in ownership or completion of new construction
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization
rows.note: Only the portion that changes ownership is reassessed. A transfer can be a sale, gift, inheritance, or trust transfer — consideration is not required.

rows.label: Operative date for the intergenerational transfer exclusion
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization
rows.note: Transfers on or before 2021-02-15 are governed by the old Proposition 58/193 rules. Transfers on or after 2021-02-16 are governed by Proposition 19.

rows.label: Implementing statute for the intergenerational transfer exclusion
rows.value: Revenue and Taxation Code section 63.2; Property Tax Rule 462.520
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization, LTA 2026/026
rows.note: Prop 19 added Article XIII A section 2.1 to the California Constitution; SB 539 (Stats. 2021, ch. 427) added R&T Code 63.2 effective 2021-09-30.

rows.label: Inflation-adjusted $1 million amount, transfers 2025-02-16 through 2027-02-15
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization, Letter To Assessors No. 2025/009
rows.note: The value cap is the property's factored base year value PLUS this amount. FHFA California House Price Index rose 2.15% in 2024, producing the adjustment. Next adjustment February 2027.

rows.label: Inflation-adjusted $1 million amount, transfers 2021-02-16 through 2023-02-15
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization, Letter To Assessors No. 2025/009
rows.note: Initial amount.

rows.label: Inflation-adjusted $1 million amount, transfers 2023-02-16 through 2025-02-15
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization, Letter To Assessors No. 2025/009
rows.note: First biennial adjustment.

rows.label: Deadline for the transferee to make the inherited home their principal residence
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization, LTA 2026/026 (Q7)
rows.note: R&T Code 63.2(a)(1)(A). The BOE states plainly: 'There are no exceptions to this rule.'

rows.label: Deadline to file the Homeowners' Exemption or Disabled Veterans' Exemption
rows.value: 1 year from date of death or transfer
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization
rows.note: Form BOE-266 (Homeowners') or BOE-261-G (Disabled Veterans'). Filed with the County Assessor. If filed after the 1-year window the exclusion is applied prospectively only.

rows.label: Deadline to file the exclusion claim (BOE-19-P)
rows.value: 3 years from date of death or transfer, or before transfer to a third party, whichever is earlier
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization

rows.label: Availability of the exclusion for inherited rental or second homes
rows.value: None — fully reassessed to fair market value
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization
rows.note: Prop 19 eliminated the exclusion for real property other than the transferor's principal residence. Prop 58/193 had allowed up to $1 million of factored base year value of other property; that is gone.

rows.label: Does holding the home in a trust change the analysis?
rows.value: No. A transfer of present beneficial ownership between parent and child qualifies 'whether within or outside a trust.'
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization, LTA 2026/026 (Definitions, item 13)
rows.note: The trust is the medium, not the answer. The residence, occupancy, value, and filing tests still apply in full.

rows.label: When does a change in ownership occur for property held in a revocable trust?
rows.value: When interests vest in persons other than the trustor or the trustor's spouse, generally on the trustor's death
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization, Proposition 19 FAQ #9 (citing R&T Code 61(h) and Rule 462.260)
rows.note: The date of death is treated as the date of change in ownership, so the law in effect on the date of death controls. For a death in the 2040-2050 window, Proposition 19 applies.

rows.label: Multi-unit building where the transferor lives in one unit
rows.value: Only the unit the transferor occupies as a principal residence qualifies as the family home; the rest is reassessed at full cash value
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization, LTA 2026/026 (Q5)
rows.note: Directly relevant to Property B, a three-unit building. Under Prop 19 only the owner-occupied unit plus its homesite would be excludable; the two rented units would be reassessed.

rows.label: What happens if the heir later moves out?
rows.value: The exclusion is removed and the new base year value is enrolled on the lien date following the loss of eligibility
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization, LTA 2026/026 (Continual Use Requirement, Q8)
rows.note: The exclusion can continue only if a different eligible transferee occupies the home as their principal residence within one year.

rows.label: Formula when fair market value exceeds the value cap
rows.value: New taxable value = factored base year value + (fair market value − excluded amount), where excluded amount = factored base year value + the adjusted $1 million amount
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization, LTA 2026/026 (Definitions, items 4, 5 and 10)
rows.note: This is a partial reassessment, not a full one. Applied on the Scenarios page.

rows.label: Principal residence value limit, former law vs current law
rows.value: Former law (Prop 58/193): no value limit. Current law (Prop 19): current taxable value plus $1,000,000 as biennially adjusted.
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization
rows.note: Prop 58/193 also required no occupancy by the child. Prop 19 added both the occupancy test and the value cap.

rows.label: Base year value transfer for owners 55+, severely disabled, or wildfire/disaster victims
rows.value: Up to 3 transfers, anywhere in California, replacement purchased or newly constructed within 2 years of sale
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization
rows.note: R&T Code 69.6, operative 2021-04-01. No value limit, but value above 'equal or lesser value' is added to the transferred base. Relevant as an alternative for the current owner, not the heir.

rows.label: Where Prop 19 claims are filed
rows.value: The County Assessor of the county where the property is located
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization
rows.note: Property A sits in Santa Clara County; Property B in the City and County of San Francisco.

rows.label: Death Statement filing requirement after a change in ownership caused by death
rows.value: File with the County Assessor within 150 days
rows.source_name: Office of the Assessor, County of Santa Clara, Annual Report 2025
rows.note: The Santa Clara County Assessor's published FAQ states the Death Statement is required even when the property was held in the decedent's trust. Shown here as the Santa Clara rule applicable to Property A.

rows.label: Homeowners' Exemption reduction in taxable value
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization, Homeowners' Exemption
rows.note: Verbatim: 'The California Constitution provides a $7,000 reduction in the taxable value for a qualifying owner-occupied home. The home must have been the principal place of residence of the owner on the lien date, January 1st.' One-time filing with the county assessor on form BOE-266. Not deducted separately in this site's projections: the effective tax rate was derived from the owner's own bill, which may already reflect it, and the effect is only about $93 a year.

rows.label: Constitutional source of the 1% rate cap and the 2% assessment growth cap
rows.value: California Constitution Article XIII A, including section 2.1 as added by Proposition 19
rows.source_name: California State Board of Equalization, LTA 2026/026 (citing Article XIII A section 2.1)
rows.note: Cited here on the authority of the BOE's own letter, which quotes Article XIII A section 2.1(c) and (c)(4) verbatim. The full text of Article XIII A was not separately retrieved in this pass.

rows.label: Statute imposing a California estate tax
rows.value: Revenue and Taxation Code section 13302 — a pick-up tax equal only to the federal Credit for State Death Taxes
rows.source_name: California Legislative Information, R&T Code 13302
rows.note: Reproduced in full on the Inheritance & Estate Tax page. Because Congress repealed the federal credit, this section computes to zero. See the flagged note there about confirming the federal repeal citation.
